newsitem.title: CHINA: French firms sign aviation deals with China.
newsitem.headline: French firms sign aviation deals with China.

text.p: Aviation Industries of China (AVIC) signed a series of agreements on Thursday with French companies including a deal with Eurocopter, a subsidiary of Aerospatiale, to develop helicopter rotors.
Other deals were an accord with SNECMA on engines and a letter of intent with Blanc Aero, officials said.
However, in a glaring omission, there was no immediate sign although officials did not rule out an agreement before President Jacques Chirac ends his visit to Beijing on Saturday.
Chirac, who witnessed, the signing ceremonies on Thursday, is due to fly to Shanghai on Saturday and leaves for home on Sunday.
Officials declined to give further details of the letter of intent between AVIC and Blanc Aero, a subsidiary of GFI Industries, saying only that it involved aeronautics.
Among the agreements signed was an industrial cooperation accord between AVIC and French state-owned aerospace group SNECMA to cooperate on engines. Officials declined to give further details.

However, the accord appeared to signal that SNECMA had won or was close to winning the contract to supply engines for the 100-seater aircraft to be developed by AVIC, Singapore and a consortium involving Airbus. Competition has been fierce to supply the engines for the regional airliner to be assembled in China.

AVIC also signed an agreement for industrial cooperation with the Aero International (Regional) consortium that groups and Finmeccanica unit, Alenia of Italy, on the ATR-72 turboprop aircraft. Officials gave no details.
The cooperation agreement with Eurocopter would be to develop 5.5 tonne helicopter rotors with AVIC, officials said.
AVIC officials refused to give details of the deals.
